column3: “as he called upon the name of the LORD” makes Moses the subject; the Hebrew “and he proclaimed the name of the LORD” may refer to the LORD.
“slow to anger” renders “long of nostrils,” and “lovingkindness and truth” renders “hesed and faithfulness (emet).”
“will by no means leave … unpunished” renders an emphatic doubled verb, and NASB supplies “the guilty”; “grandchildren” renders “children of children.”
“even though … so obstinate” renders “for it is a people stiff of neck.”
“God said” renders “he said”; “miracles” renders “wonders,” “produced” renders “created,” and “fearful” renders “awesome.”
“worship” renders “bow down to”; NASB sets the verse off with dashes.
“play the harlot with” renders “prostitute themselves after” (also in verse 16).
“male livestock” renders an unusual Hebrew form; the meaning is uncertain.
“at the turn of the year” renders “at the circuit of the year.”
“in accordance with” renders “on the mouth of.”
“bread” renders “food (lechem),” and “the Ten Commandments” renders “the ten words.”
NASB puts the clause about the two tablets in parentheses.
